item.title: CISA Warns on Exploited Fortinet FortiSandbox and SharePoint RCE Flaws
item.content:encoded:
CISA Adds Exploited SharePoint RCE Zero-Day CVE-2026-58644 to KEV — Must Read

CISA added a newly patched Microsoft SharePoint Server zero-day, CVE-2026-58644, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation, requiring U.S. federal agencies to patch by July 19, 2026. Organizations running on-premises SharePoint should urgently apply updates, verify defenses like AMSI, and check for signs of compromise.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-58644, a newly patched Microsoft SharePoint Server flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and required Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to apply fixes by July 19, 2026.
  • CVE-2026-58644 is a critical deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.8 that allows an unauthorized attacker to execute arbitrary code.
  • Microsoft said the vulnerability can be exploited remotely over the internet and has low attack complexity because attackers need no significant prior system knowledge and can repeatedly succeed with a payload against the vulnerable component.
  • The vulnerability affects Microsoft SharePoint Server Subscription Edition, Microsoft SharePoint Server 2019, and Microsoft SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016.
  • CISA warned that multiple SharePoint Server vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-58644, are being actively exploited to gain unauthorized access to on-premises instances and support post-exploitation activity such as stealing IIS machine keys and deploying malware.

CISA urges immediate action on actively exploited Fortinet flaws — Must Read

CISA says two critical Fortinet FortiSandbox flaws are being actively exploited and has ordered U.S. federal agencies to patch affected systems by July 19. The vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated remote code execution via command injection, so admins should upgrade immediately.

  • CISA ordered U.S. government agencies to prioritize patching two actively exploited critical vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiSandbox, tracked as CVE-2026-39808 and CVE-2026-25089.
  • Fortinet addressed CVE-2026-39808 on April 14 and CVE-2026-25089 on June 9, and administrators must upgrade affected deployments to the latest released versions to block attacks.
  • Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated threat actors to remotely execute unauthorized code through low-complexity command injection attacks that require no user interaction.
  • Threat intelligence company Defused reported on June 16 that attackers had begun exploiting multiple Fortinet FortiSandbox vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-39808 and CVE-2026-25089, in the wild.
  • CISA added the two flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and requires U.S. federal agencies to patch vulnerable FortiSandbox instances by Sunday, July 19.

US charges two over laundering $43 million from investment fraud — Should Read

U.S. prosecutors charged Zhuoying Chen and Haojie Zhang with laundering at least $43 million stolen from cyber investment fraud victims through 140 bank accounts and dozens of shell companies. If convicted of money-laundering conspiracy, they face up to 20 years in prison.

  • U.S. prosecutors charged Zhuoying Chen and Haojie Zhang for their alleged roles in a crime ring that laundered money stolen in cyber investment fraud scams.
  • Chen and Zhang allegedly managed a network of more than a dozen people in Queens and Brooklyn between 2020 and 2022.
  • The indictment alleges the network moved at least $43 million in scam proceeds to bank accounts in China using 140 bank accounts under roughly 45 shell companies.
  • The underlying scams involved criminals contacting victims through social media or messaging services, building trust, showing fake profits, and stealing additional money invested in the schemes.
  • If convicted of conspiracy to commit money laundering, Chen and Zhang face a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison.

Windows Server 2022 reach end of mainstream support in 90 days — May Read

Windows Server 2022 will leave mainstream support on October 13, 2026, but will continue receiving free monthly security updates under extended support until October 14, 2031. Microsoft is urging customers to plan upgrades to Windows Server 2025 for full mainstream support.

  • Microsoft announced that Windows Server 2022 will reach the end of mainstream support on October 13, 2026.
  • After October 13, 2026, Windows Server 2022 will move to extended support and continue receiving monthly security updates at no additional cost through October 14, 2031.
  • Microsoft advises customers to plan upgrades to Windows Server 2025, the latest Long-Term Servicing Channel release for Windows Server.
  • Windows Server 2025 became generally available in November 2024 and is scheduled to receive mainstream support until November 13, 2029, with extended support ending on November 14, 2034.
  • Microsoft also extended Windows Server 2022 hotpatching until October 2027 for systems running Datacenter: Azure Edition.
